module

public import Mathlib.NumberTheory.AlmostPrime


@[expose] public section

namespace Nat

instance (k n : ℕ) : Decidable (IsAlmostPrime k n) := by unfold IsAlmostPrime; infer_instance

instance (k n : ℕ) : Decidable (IsAtMostAlmostPrime k n) := by
  unfold IsAtMostAlmostPrime; infer_instance

end Nat

reformulations.difference: This indirect use site subtracts one from the indices in the OEIS comment: for example, Lean asserts primality at a(8) and semiprimality at a(9), whereas the comment labels these positions a(9) and a(10).
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The OEIS entry declares offset 0, and its displayed data place 2 at index 8 and 6 at index 9. Its comment instead numbers positions from 1. Writing b(m) = a(m - 1) for positive m translates every prime/semiprime assertion in the comment exactly into the Lean conjunction. The full reindexed conjunction was proved equivalent by reflexivity in /workspace/review/use_sites.lean; computations also confirmed the initial sequence values.

review.notes: No mathematical defects found. The target declares only two Decidable instances for predicates imported directly from Mathlib; it introduces no alternative almost-prime definition. Both instances correctly decide the nonzero, multiplicity-counting predicates, and no duplicate Mathlib instances were found. Scratch proofs establish equivalence with products of exactly k primes, the at-most/exact relationship, and the two-prime characterization of semiprimes. Tests cover 0, 1, prime squares, prime cubes, and witnesses for every k. All five semiprime use sites agree with their sources. Additional Lean checks prove A114137(0) = 8 and nonemptiness of the odd-semiprime set above every bound. Both scratch files compile successfully. Direct OEIS requests were blocked, so its official data export dated 2026-09-07 was used. The cited A100474 proof matches the recorded answer and least index 36. All experiments are under /workspace/review/; the target file was not changed.
